transitions.historical_text: Increase the ATK of a monster equipped with this card by 1000 points. When this card is sent from the field to the Graveyard, if you Tribute 1 monster on your side of the field, this card returns to the top of your Deck.
transitions.summary: Era trigger timing, not a text erratum: the GOAT script adds EFFECT_FLAG_DELAY to the send-to-Deck trigger (upstream comment 'Doesn't miss timing'), so the optional 'When this card is sent from the field to the Graveyard' effect can still be activated when its trigger is not the last thing to have happened; the modern script omits DELAY and the effect misses timing. No printed text in the lineage carries this difference and no dated source for the change was found, so the chronology is unresolved.

transitions.summary: Wording only, on period rulings (round 037, 2026-09-29). The record claimed: (c2, 2013 erratum) Modern: '(This card is always treated as an "Archfiend" card.)', so cards keyed on 'Archfiend' count Axe of Despair. The record says the era card was not an Archfiend. A period ruling in force says otherwise: Konami TCG Card FAQ default_fh page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "The Archfiend you need for "Falling Down" doesn't have to be a monster. Cards like "Axe of Despair", or an Archfiend monster equipped to your "Relinquished", will prevent "Falling Down" from being destroyed." No difference between the era card and the modern card is established.

review.notes:
Second script hunk is a no-op: the goat 'Duel.SendtoDeck(c,nil,0,REASON_EFFECT)' uses the literal 0, and constant.lua:28 defines SEQ_DECKTOP = 0, so it is identical to the modern SEQ_DECKTOP call. ERA MISMATCH on the cdb side: I queried both databases - goat-entries.cdb 504700068 and cards.cdb 40619825 both carry setcode 69 (0x45, Archfiend), so the GOAT variant already grants the 2013 'Archfiend' treatment about nine years early. It is behaviourally inert for GOAT/Edison (no period card keys on 'Archfiend' Spell cards), but the record should not pretend the historical entry is clean. No intermediate implementation is proposed between the undated ruling change and the 2013 functional change: the ruling change's chronology is unresolved, and both project snapshots (2005-04-01, 2010-04-24) precede 2013-06-28, so only the baseline is ever selected. Trailing cosmetics after v6: v7 (YS14-EN026, 2014-07-10, 'place this card on the top of your Deck') and v8 (LART-EN051, 2022-12-16, GY). The pinned modern cdb text matches v7 at 0.9976 (a line break after the parenthetical), not v8.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Axe of Despair). A period ruling in force contradicts every difference the transition claimed: (c2, 2013 erratum) Modern: '(This card is always treated as an "Archfiend" card.)', so cards keyed on 'Archfiend' count Axe of Despair. The record says the era card was not an Archfiend. Contradicted by Konami TCG Card FAQ default_fh page (Internet Archive capture served 2008-12-15): "The Archfiend you need for "Falling Down" doesn't have to be a monster. Cards like "Axe of Despair", or an Archfiend monster equipped to your "Relinquished", will prevent "Falling Down" from being destroyed." Upper Deck Entertainment official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings page (Internet Archive replay): "The Archfiend you need for "Falling Down" doesn't have to be a monster. Cards like "Axe of Despair", or an Archfiend monster equipped to your "Relinquished", will prevent "Falling Down" from being destroyed." The transition is cosmetic: no difference between the era card and the modern card is established. Verdicts: [c2] d1 contradicted at Edison, contradicted at Tengu. Variant-script points a ruling contradicts, listed for the owner (Ignis's script is not edited): Axe of Despair: the variant script (from the undated c0 ruling event, left alone) can return the card even after its trigger missed timing; the card FAQ (after Cyber Jar) says the timing has passed. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "The BP02 printing added '(This card is always treated as an "Archfiend" card.)', giving the TCG card membership of the 'Archfiend' archetype that it did not previously have; any card keying on 'Archfiend' by name treats Axe of Despair differently before and after this printing. Archetype membership is carried by the cdb setcode rather than the Lua script, so it does not appear in the script diff."
